purpose: Let a reader browse every blog article, newest first, and narrow the list by category: a filter row followed by a vertical list of article cards, the first one drawn larger as the featured article.

behaviour.note: Data is a static snapshot of 43 articles (28 Tips, 12 Tech, 2 Customer Story, 1 Company), already ordered newest first; the list is not re-sorted in code. Excerpts in this clone are neutral one-line summaries written for the clone, not the original copy, and the article body pages use placeholder text.

Category filter: All, Company, Tips, Tech, Customer Story, shown as radio-like square markers (filled square with a small white dot when active). The active category is kept in the URL as ?category=<lowercased label> (for example customer story with the space encoded); choosing All removes the parameter. Matching is case-insensitive on the post category. The URL is the only filter state, so a filtered view is linkable and survives reload.

Changing the filter does not reset the page scroll position (preventScrollReset). An unrecognised category value yields an empty list with no empty-state message; the filter row then shows no active item.
Filters are hidden below 600px (the sm breakpoint): on a phone there is no filter row and the full unfiltered list shows (a ?category= value in the URL still filters it, invisibly).

Featured layout: the first card of the current (possibly filtered) list uses the featured layout (wider image column, larger 24px title, 1400px image request); every other card is standard (20px title, 900px image request). So with a filter active, the first match becomes the featured card.

Each card: square cover image, a category chip, a bold title that is the link (the whole card is clickable through a stretched pseudo-element on the title link), a one-sentence excerpt, a mono uppercase date and a small square author avatar, then a hairline divider. Hovering the card fades the cover image to 90% over 200ms.

The last two words of every excerpt are joined with a non-breaking space to avoid a one-word last line. Dates on this index are formatted in the viewer's local time zone as short month, day, year; the article page uses UTC, so the same post can show a different day near midnight.

Author avatar images come from the AUTHORS map (5 named authors) and use the person-portrait role; alt text is the author name plus the word photo. Cover images are the blog-cover role, one distinct file per post; the cover alt text is the post title.
PostCard is shared: the same component renders the You might also like rows on article pages (see content.related-posts), always in standard, non-featured form.
Sits directly under hero.page-header on /blog (an eyebrow, headline banner written inline in the page); it is the last block before the footer and has no closing call to action.

themeDependency.how: Default light theme on the plain background; filter markers use gray-2 (inactive) and the strong text colour (active), text turns from gray-6 to gray-8 on hover. No dark scope.

variants.name: featured-card
variants.description: First card of the list: image column 5 of 12 at md, 8 of 24 at lg, 6 of 24 at xl; larger title.

variants.name: standard-card
variants.description: All later cards: narrower image column (4 of 12 at md, 6 of 24 at lg, 4 of 24 at xl) and 20px title.

categories.note: Filter labels; the first is the All reset. Observed 5.

slug.note: URL slug; the card links to /blog/<slug>.

title.note: Bold card title and cover alt text. Observed up to 23 words.

category.note: Shown in the chip and matched by the filter.

date.note: ISO timestamp; rendered as short month, day, year.

author.note: Must be a key of the authors map so an avatar exists.

cover.note: Square article cover; existing real file only.

excerpt.note: One-sentence summary. Observed up to 31 words.

takeaways.note: Not shown on the list; count of Key takeaways bullets on the article (0, 2 or 3). Belongs to the same record.

related.note: Not shown on the list; slugs of the 2 related posts used by the article page.

authorAvatars.note: One portrait per named author (5 observed), used at 24px in the card footer.

motion.reducedMotionNote: Proposal only; the code has no prefers-reduced-motion handling. Proposed: drop the 200ms fades and change state instantly.
